translation.english_title: When the people rise, the sceptre rises

english_lines: Man: When the people rise, the sceptre rises,
When the sceptre rises, the people rise,
What heights — how beautifully, in how many ways,
Our people are dying,
They are cooking in burning fire.
notes: `குடி / கோல்` is kept as `people / sceptre`, preserving the source's political reversal rather than generalizing it into abstract governance language.
The printed `ஆண்` role remains inside the first source/English line under the printed `பல்லவி` structure.
`வேகிறார்` remains the harsh bodily image `cooking` in fire rather than being softened to generic suffering.

english_lines: 'Everyone is a king of this country,' he said in the song,
Our king lives in a mud-clod house,
If thunder strikes, if rain pours,
All the kings are on the road,
Even a `sirukodindha` bird has a nest, appa,
(People rise).
notes: The colloquial `பாட்டுல / வீட்டுல / ரோட்டுல` register is kept in direct spoken English rather than formalized.
The verified source form `சிறுகொடிந்த` is not silently corrected to a familiar bird/wing expression; `sirukodindha` is therefore retained as an explicit pressure point.

english_lines: We too have feeling,
In our bungalow there is a mattress,
We drink the sour-kaadi liquor,
Husband and wife do come together,
When light is thrown, when a car comes,
We move aside, move aside, and lie down....
(People rise).
notes: `பங்களா` remains `bungalow`, preserving the source's bitterly comic contrast rather than explaining the social setting inside the lyric.
`புளிச்சக்காடி` is retained conservatively as `sour-kaadi`; the verified source form is not replaced with a guessed modern beverage label.
The repeated `விலகி விலகி` remains repeated `move aside, move aside`.

english_lines: All pearls are nose-mucus,
A blood-wound, they say, is a gem,
Diamonds are stars,
The rainbow itself is vaiduriyam.. how....
notes: The deliberately degrading pearl/mucus and wound/gem reversals are left explicit.
`வைடூரியம்` remains `vaiduriyam` rather than being narrowed to one English gem name, preserving the source term.

english_lines: Kuthuk-kallu is the throne,
The garbage bin is the kingdom,
For the people who survive by dying,
There is power to destroy the world,
(People rise).
notes: `குத்துக் கல்லு` is retained as `kuthuk-kallu` because the compact source form does not support one uniquely safe English object label without interpretation.
`செத்துப் பிழைக்கும்` remains the paradox `survive by dying`; its social-political violence is not softened.

translator_notes: This two-page song uses kingship language, homelessness, bodily ridicule, gem inversions and apocalyptic political force; the English preserves the satire rather than converting it into explanatory prose.
PDF provenance remains one continuous record across pages 90–91.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
